title: Bargara Reef Phase 3: oblique aerial of the headland with the four work zones marked (page render, 300 dpi, crop of Figure 1)
citation: Jackson, L.A. and Corbett, B. (2007). Review of Existing Multi-Functional Artificial Reefs. Australasian Conference on Coasts and Ports 2007, International Coastal Management, Queensland (authors L.A. Jackson and B.B. Corbett), p. 1, Figure 1 "Bargara Reef Phase 3 [Source: Greg Redgard]". https://ref.coastalrestorationtrust.org.nz/site/assets/files/7954/2007_cp-review_mfar.pdf. Accessed 2026-10-10.
page_or_figure: p.1 Figure 1 (embedded image xref 86, native 465x285 px; render 300 dpi)
image_date: unknown (photo of the headland, before the Phase 3 works; text of 2007 paper: "additional works have been designed [Figure 1]" citing Redgard 2006)
credit: Greg Redgard (photo and annotations), reproduced in Jackson and Corbett 2007
license: not stated (conference paper; private copy)
shows: Oblique aerial looking west-north-west over the north side of the Burkitts headland: two rock groynes at the top, a sand-floored rock pool inside the near wall, dark basalt rock flat, a breaking wave line along the platform edge; arrows/ellipse mark: reprofile several surface rocks, remove (ellipse) to lengthen break, improve shore break, reprofile dangerous rocks.
state_shown: design: Phase 3 planned work zones on the natural platform (state before those works)
how_used: 2026-10-10: the ONLY source found that locates reshaped-boulder work areas. Three ground control points (outer tip of rock wall B, its south root, outer tip of groyne A) fitted an affine map onto the Esri Wayback 2016-07-31 frame; the drawn ellipse and the four arrow tips were mapped (scripts/phase3_zone_georef.py, scripts/phase3_zone_v1.json). Ellipse = about 1,750 m2 (43 x 52 m), position +-20-30 m (LOW). Phase 3 = later "designed" additional works; not the same as the Feb 1997 first works (not located).
rights_note: Private research copy; reuse rights to be checked before any public release.
